title: I tried Perplexity as my Android assistant instead of Gemini
excerpt: I set Perplexity as my Galaxy S24 Ultra's default assistant. It handled alarms, calls, and phone controls almost as well as Gemini, with a few gaps.
content_html:
Published Nov 19, 2026, 11:00 AM EST

Haroun authors features for Android Police, covering Samsung, Google, and the wider Android ecosystem. He first joined in 2021, cutting his teeth on over 300 news stories before moving on to features and how-tos. A one-time OnePlus die-hard who genuinely couldn't stand Samsung, he's since done a full about-face — he now daily-drives a Galaxy S24 Ultra and keeps an S23+, S22+, and his old S20 within arm's reach, which gives him a lot of hardware to put through its paces.

He's a medical doctor with a decade-plus obsession for consumer tech, and his coverage has also appeared on How-To Geek and Android Authority. When he's not buried in Google's apps or a Samsung settings menu, he's trying to get his chess rating past 1500 or playing table tennis/football.

Earlier this month, I used ChatGPT and Claude as the default assistants on my Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, and the results were mixed.

ChatGPT was really poor, failing even at basic tasks like setting an alarm. Claude was better at those, but still couldn't do things like turn on my flashlight or Do Not Disturb (DND).

With Samsung building Perplexity AI into its phones, like the Galaxy S26, I wanted to see what the tool can do currently, especially on older phones that may not get that integration.

The results were surprising: Perplexity aced almost everything Gemini does well and even surpassed it in one instance.

Let me explain.

Perplexity handles basic tasks almost as well as Gemini

Alarms, timers, and reminders right inside your apps

I asked Perplexity to set timers, alarms, and reminders, and it did so seamlessly.

This contrasted sharply with my previous test, where Claude couldn't set a reminder and had to create an alarm, and ChatGPT couldn't do any of those.

I pushed further by asking Perplexity to save some items to my (non-existent) shopping list. It created a reminder and asked when I wanted to be reminded.

Gemini's execution was better because it opened Google Keep and pulled up old to-do lists I didn't remember I still had. But Perplexity wasn't doing badly by any means.

It makes calls, drafts emails, and manages your calendar

I wanted to see how well Perplexity could connect with communication apps, if at all.

I asked it to call my cousin. Like Gemini, it asked me which number to use, with both of his contacts showing up on the assistant interface.

I also asked it to email my landlord about a leaking sink, and it drafted one in Gmail, signed off with my name, and asked who to send it to.

It also read out my calendar events for the next day and added a new event.

It controls basic phone features

Both ChatGPT and Claude failed this in my previous test, so I wanted to see how Perplexity would perform.

I first asked it to turn on my flashlight, expecting an error message. But it actually turned it on.

When I asked it to book an Uber to the airport, it opened Uber's site inside Chrome with the airport set as my destination.

The one thing it didn't do was turn on DND. But even then, it took me to the DND option within Settings, and I only had to toggle it on.

Perplexity beats Gemini on this one thing

All answers come with sources

One of Perplexity's biggest selling points is its citations for almost every query. That was very much on show in its assistant mode.

It gave government sources when I asked for the capital of Australia and cited AccuWeather when I asked for the weather in Chicago the next day.

It also provided sources for seemingly simple things, like converting 350 degrees Fahrenheit to Celsius and translating a sentence into Spanish.

Even when summarizing one of our articles displayed on my screen, it added citations to Android Police. It's a useful feature, so it's no surprise that even open source Perplexity alternatives copy it.

Where Perplexity falls short

It can't send texts

This was a strange one because Perplexity showed it could call and draft emails.

However, when I asked it to text my cousin, it tried and failed to find a messaging app, even though Google Messages is my default for SMS.

Then it directed me to the Galaxy Store to download Google Messages, but that failed because the app isn't available in Samsung's store.

When I repeated the command, it wrote me a draft and suggested connecting to Outlook to send it.

It's not good with nearby places

This was another strange one with Perplexity.

When I asked for directions to the nearest pharmacy, it opened a Google Maps route to an unlabeled place about nine miles away. On the retry, it said it couldn't identify a pharmacy.

For context, neither ChatGPT nor Claude could open Maps in my previous test. But they both pointed me to the nearest pharmacy.

Meanwhile, Perplexity launched Maps, but didn't really do much with it.

I found a Google Maps (Places API) connector among the available Perplexity plugins, but that requires a paid subscription.

It's not hands-free

One of Gemini's biggest advantages over other AI assistants is the "Hey Google" wake word that lets you activate it without touching your phone.

Like ChatGPT and Claude, Perplexity lacks one.

The Galaxy S26 launched with a "Hey Plex" wake word that was removed in an early update, but Perplexity says it's coming back as "Hey Perplexity."

That should solve the problem for Galaxy S26 owners.

Perplexity is the best Gemini alternative yet

I wasn't expecting Perplexity to be this good at controlling my phone.

It makes calls, drafts emails, and turns on your flashlight. It can even do half the job of booking an Uber ride for you.

There are current or upcoming workarounds for where it fails. The paid version gives you a Maps connector, and the Galaxy S26 will get its wake word back.

Gemini is still on top, but Perplexity is a very close second that genuinely works.

If you're not sure which AI tool to use, we tested every assistant on Android to find the best one.
